memory_candidates.content: When a proposed change targets a decision predicate consumed by a proof, the soundness question is often not 'is the new predicate correct?' but 'does the proof read the predicate's content at all, or only the control-flow shape of the match it drives?'. In CSLib's intuitionistic tableau, intExpandBranches_closed_unsat's reuse arm passes the branch, edges, and world counter through completely unchanged and discards the witness label with an underscore at the go-loop call site -- so the proof plausibly depends only on which match arm was taken, not on why. The historical failure of the alternative fix is the confirming signal: it broke soundness precisely because it MODIFIED the branch on the reuse path, invalidating an already-established satisfaction witness, not because its predicate was wrong. Planning heuristic: before scoping a predicate-swap spike, first check whether the consuming proof mentions the predicate's spec lemma or the structure being restated at all -- an empty dependency cone converts an expensive proof-repair question into a cheap shape-preservation check, and sharply reduces the spike's phase count.
